data.description:
## Description

**What**: Round-trip integration test suite that asserts local-CREATE → outbound → mocked Jira REST v3 GET → inbound → local-state preserves description content and assignee identity end-to-end. Includes a 4-case failure-injection matrix where each fix is independently reverted and the suite must produce a diagnostic test failure naming the specific silent-drop path. At least one test case drives the actual shell/workflow entry point (not the Python module directly).

**Why**: Without regression coverage tied to the specific failure modes, the next incomplete fix or refactor will reintroduce one of these silent-drop paths and ship undetected — the chronic pattern the user described. The failure-injection matrix is the empirical proof that the test suite actually catches each bug class, not a generic "tests exist" assertion.

**Scope**:
- IN: pytest-style integration test suite in tests/ directory, mocked Jira REST v3 endpoints (responses fixture or similar), 4 failure-injection cases (cursor revert, env_id revert, ADF isinstance revert, null-assignee revert), at least one shell-entry-point test case (invokes the actual workflow script with subprocess + git fixture), CI integration (test must run in existing CI workflow).
- OUT: production Jira sandbox testing (no live Jira account stand-up — mocks only), end-to-end browser test (no UI involved), benchmarking.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the round-trip test suite covers local-CREATE → outbound → mocked Jira v3 GET → inbound → local-state and asserts both description text and assignee identity are preserved across the round-trip ← Satisfies: "A round-trip integration test asserts local-CREATE → outbound → mocked Jira REST v3 GET → inbound → local-state preserves description text and assignee identity end-to-end"
- When this story is complete, the failure-injection matrix has 4 independent test cases, each reverting exactly one fix (cursor, env_id, ADF isinstance, null-assignee) and asserting the suite fails with a diagnostic identifying the specific silent-drop path — the four reverts MUST NOT be combinable into a single test ← Satisfies: SC5 (failure-injection clause)
- When this story is complete, at least one test case invokes the actual workflow entry-point script (subprocess against the cron entry-point with a fixture git repo containing 3+ back-to-back commits older than HEAD~1) and asserts all 3 commits' events reach the mocked Jira endpoint ← Satisfies: SC5 (shell-entry-point clause)
- When this story is complete, the test suite runs in CI on every PR touching the bridge code paths (plugins/dso/scripts/bridge*.py, .github/workflows/*-bridge.yml) and is REQUIRED to pass before merge ← Satisfies: SC5 (regression-detection-on-merge property)
- When this story is complete, the test suite is documented in plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/README or equivalent so future contributors know which test to update when adding a bridge feature ← Satisfies: scrutiny consideration on test maintainability

## Considerations

- [Testing] Mock Jira responses must be schema-faithful (real ADF JSON dict, real accountId UUID, real issue key format) — derived from a recorded sandbox response, not contrived.
- [Reliability] The shell-entry-point test must isolate its working directory (mktemp under /tmp following CLAUDE.md rule 16) and clean up via trap to avoid CI workspace pollution.
- [Maintainability] Each failure-injection case should be a separate pytest function, not parametrized — making CI failure messages name the specific bug class (e.g., test_cursor_revert_drops_old_commits).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a maintainer, a round-trip integration test detects regressions of any of the four silent-drop fixes via a failure-injection matrix
